title: Protect the access layer
blurb: Stop rogue DHCP servers, ARP spoofing and MAC flooding with DHCP snooping, DAI and port security.
purpose: Most attacks against the access layer need nothing more than a cable. This lab turns on DHCP snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection and port security, which together stop rogue DHCP servers, ARP spoofing and MAC flooding. It covers the Layer 2 security features SCOR expects you to configure.
scenario: Users in **VLAN 10** on switch SW1 report that they sometimes get the wrong default gateway. Someone plugged a home router into a desk port, and it's handing out addresses. Harden SW1: only the uplink **GigabitEthernet1/0/48** leads to the real DHCP server, and desk port **GigabitEthernet1/0/5** should allow at most **2** devices.
topology:
DHCP server ── Gi1/0/48 [SW1] Gi1/0/5 ── desk (PC + IP phone)
                 (trusted)       (untrusted, VLAN 10)
objectives: Turn on DHCP snooping for VLAN 10 and trust the uplink
Turn on Dynamic ARP Inspection, which relies on the snooping table
Limit the desk port with port security
Pick the right violation mode and verify the bindings

steps.title: DHCP snooping
steps.learn: **DHCP snooping** splits ports into **trusted** (toward real DHCP servers) and **untrusted** (everything else). Server messages such as OFFER and ACK that arrive on an untrusted port are dropped. The switch also builds a **binding table** of MAC, IP, VLAN and port from the leases it sees.
steps.task: Turn on DHCP snooping globally and for **VLAN 10**, then trust the uplink **GigabitEthernet1/0/48**.
steps.hint: `ip dhcp snooping`, `ip dhcp snooping vlan 10`, then `interface GigabitEthernet1/0/48` and `ip dhcp snooping trust`.

commands.explain: Turns on DHCP snooping for VLAN 10.
Enters the uplink toward the real DHCP server.

commands.note: Only the uplink may send DHCP server messages now.
commands.explain: Trusts DHCP server messages on this port only. Server replies on any other port are dropped.

steps.title: Where did the rogue OFFER go?
steps.question: The home router on Gi1/0/5 sends a DHCPOFFER. What does SW1 do with it?

options.text: Drops it, because Gi1/0/5 is untrusted and an OFFER is a server message.
Forwards it, because the client asked for an address.
options.why: Untrusted ports may send client messages (DISCOVER, REQUEST) but not server messages.
Snooping drops the packet. It doesn't err-disable the port unless you add a rate limit that's exceeded.

steps.title: Dynamic ARP Inspection
steps.learn: **DAI** checks ARP packets on untrusted ports against the DHCP snooping binding table and drops replies that claim someone else's IP address. That stops ARP spoofing and man-in-the-middle attacks. The uplink is trusted, just as it is for snooping.
steps.task: Turn on ARP inspection for **VLAN 10** and trust it on **GigabitEthernet1/0/48**.
steps.hint: `ip arp inspection vlan 10`, then on the uplink `ip arp inspection trust`.

commands.explain: Turns on Dynamic ARP Inspection for VLAN 10, which checks ARP against the snooping table.
Trusts ARP on the uplink so ARP from the rest of the network isn't checked twice.

steps.title: Port security on the desk port
steps.learn: **Port security** limits how many MAC addresses a port learns, which defeats MAC flooding and unapproved hubs. **Sticky** learning saves the first addresses it sees into the running configuration.
steps.task: On **GigabitEthernet1/0/5**: make it an access port, turn on port security, allow a **maximum of 2** addresses, use **sticky** learning, and set the violation mode to **restrict**.
steps.hint: `interface GigabitEthernet1/0/5`, `switchport mode access`, `switchport port-security`, `switchport port-security maximum 2`, `switchport port-security mac-address sticky`, `switchport port-security violation restrict`.

commands.note: Port security needs a static access (or trunk) port, not a dynamic one.
commands.explain: Makes the port an access port, which port security requires.
Allows at most 2 MAC addresses, for example a phone and a PC.
Learns the connected MAC addresses and saves them to the configuration.
Drops traffic from extra MAC addresses and logs it, but keeps the port up.

steps.title: Match the violation modes
steps.learn: All three modes drop frames from the extra MAC address. They differ in whether they log it, and whether the port stays up.
steps.task: Match each violation mode to what it does.

fields.label: protect
options: Drops silently, no log or counter
Drops, logs and counts, port stays up
fields.answer: Drops silently, no log or counter

fields.label: restrict
options: Drops silently, no log or counter
Drops, logs and counts, port stays up
fields.answer: Drops, logs and counts, port stays up

fields.label: shutdown (default)
options: Drops silently, no log or counter
Drops, logs and counts, port stays up

steps.title: Verify the bindings
steps.task: Display the DHCP snooping binding table.

commands.output:

commands.note: These bindings are what DAI checks ARP replies against.
commands.explain: Shows the DHCP snooping table of MAC, IP, VLAN and port that DAI checks against.

summary: DHCP snooping on VLAN 10 with a trusted uplink, Dynamic ARP Inspection using the snooping bindings, and port security limiting the desk port to two sticky MAC addresses in restrict mode.
